subject: Re: NexaHealth - rollback guarantee & pin policy for canary
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nexahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: NexaHealth - rollback guarantee & pin policy for canary

Team —

NexaHealth asked us this morning for a formalized rollback / "pin" guarantee as part of their launch next week. They want written confirmation that during a canary/A-B rollout we will:

- Run a 6–12 hour canary at 5% traffic, configurable to 10% on mutual agreement.
- Automatically revert all traffic to the previously pinned model variant if p95 latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR if 5xx rate > 1% for the same period.
- Preserve the pinned model variant for at least 24 hours after a revert to allow forensic checks (they want a guarantee we won't accidentally continue on the degraded variant).

They've asked for this as a formal SLA exception in their contract (they're sensitive about tails because they generate clinical summaries). Attached is the SLA exception form they sent (sla-exception-form.pdf).

Questions for sign-off:
1) Is the auto-revert rule above safe operationally?
2) Does pinning the previous variant for 24h create any service constraints on our Dedicated pools we need to surface to Sales/Legal?
3) Who will be the rollout owner and who needs to be on-call during the canary window?

My recommendation: approve with the auto-revert thresholds above, require on-call alerting (pager to infra rotation), and add a 2-hour manual hold window for any rollback that requires human validation. Marcus — can you own the rollout and validate the auto-revert config? Rishi/Marissa — need approval from Eng Ops and Sales for the contractual language.

I plan to respond to Sarah with a proposed timeline once we have internal sign-offs.

— Ava

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NexaHealth - rollback guarantee & pin policy for canary

Agree with Ava's proposal with two additions:

- Require an on-call alert that triggers an automated diagnostic scrub and posts a short summary to the rollout channel (rollout: #nexahealth-canary) so we can make a fast call if the auto-revert happens.
- Define a soft SLO credit cap in the amendment: if auto-revert occurs within the first 12h, customer gets a 5% credit; after 12h no automatic credit but we escalate for a postmortem. Legal can finalize numbers.

Operationally the auto-revert thresholds look good. Pinning for 24h should be fine — we just need to be explicit in the amendment that the pinned variant consumes reserved capacity and may block autoscaling for that pool until the pin is released.

Marcus: please prepare the auto-revert config (YAML) and a short runbook for the canary. If we can attach the config to the amendment, Legal can sign it off faster.

-r

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NexaHealth - rollback guarantee & pin policy for canary

Thanks — I can own the rollout. A couple of clarifying points before I publish the config:

- Auto-revert window: do we want "3 consecutive 5-min windows" (15 minutes) or a longer safety window (e.g., 30 minutes) given downstream cache warming / KV pressure on med-summaries? Short window reduces exposure but increases risk of flip-flopping.
- Pin semantics: should the pin be "hard" (block any new deployments to that model slot) or "soft" (allow pin but permit emergency hotfixes via an override token)? Legal usually prefers hard pins but on-prem customers sometimes need an override path.

Proposed compromise: 15-min auto-revert, 24h hard pin but with an override token that requires two approvers (one Eng Ops + one Sales leader). That lets us unblock a true emergency without materially exposing the customer.

Attached is the first pass of the auto-revert config. It's minimal and references our standard autoscaler labels and alerting hooks.

(attachment: auto-revert-config.yaml)

— Marcus

Subject: Re: NexaHealth - rollback guarantee & pin policy for canary

Sarah / NexaHealth team —

Thanks for your patience. Internal approvals are in place to proceed with the requested canary guard rails. Summary of the agreed terms (for the amendment):

- Canary: 5% traffic for initial 6–12h (can extend to 10% by mutual agreement).
- Auto-revert: triggered if p95 latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows (15 minutes total) OR 5xx > 1% for same period.
- Pin: previous model variant will be pinned for 24 hours after an automatic revert.
- Override: we will allow a hard-pin override but it requires two approvers (one Eng Ops + one Sales director).
- On-call & alerts: Eng Ops will page and publish an automated diagnostic summary to #nexahealth-canary. Marcus will be rollout owner.
- Credits: If an auto-revert occurs in the first 12h, Redwood will apply a 5% usage credit per the amendment.

Next steps:
1) I've attached the signed SLA exception form with these agreed terms. Please confirm acceptance and we'll send a DocuSign amendment for signatures.
2) Marcus will schedule the canary and post the runbook + auto-revert YAML to the rollout channel.
3) Legal will attach the capacity note about pinned variants to the amendment.

If that all looks good I will send the formal DocuSign link.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
